invariant_facts.context: Two project coordinators are jointly preparing a client presentation and had agreed on a review cutoff for changes to the slide deck.
invariant_facts.conflict_trigger: The addressee changed the slide deck after the agreed review cutoff without informing the speaker.
invariant_facts.source_of_disagreement: The late uncommunicated changes caused the speaker to redo work that had already been completed.
invariant_facts.organizational_consequence: The duplicated work increased coordination costs before the next project deadline.

evaluation_question: Assess conflict severity, aggression, cooperativeness, attribution of responsibility, appropriate conflict-management strategy, escalation level, and a suitable managerial response.

DC.message: You changed the slide deck after our review cutoff without telling me. That made me redo work I had already finished. We need to agree how we communicate late changes before the next deadline.

DI.message: You revised the slide deck after the agreed review cutoff without notifying me. This resulted in duplicated work on my side. We need to establish a process for communicating late-stage changes before the next deadline.

MC.message: I wanted to flag that you changed the slide deck after our review cutoff without telling me, which meant I had to redo work I had already finished. Could we agree on how to communicate late changes before the next deadline?

MI.message: I wanted to raise that you revised the slide deck after the agreed review cutoff without notifying me, which resulted in duplicated work on my side. Could we establish a process for communicating late-stage changes before the next deadline?
